commit_message:
Bug 1961424 - Store CachedBAxisMeasurement's key verbatim instead of hashing them. r=emilio

Instead of bit-packing grid area inline size and baseline padding into a hash,
store them as separate fields to avoid key collisions.

I failed to craft a testcase to cover this change alone. However, with the new
behavior introduced in bug 1944423 (with
`layout.css.grid-multi-pass-track-sizing.enabled` enabled), these WPTs will fail
without this patch.

- css/css-grid/layout-algorithm/grid-fit-content-percentage.html
- css/css-grid/layout-algorithm/grid-container-percentage-001.html

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D246465

fix_commit.message: Bug 1965081 - Ensure CachedBAxisMeasurement is valid before accessing it. r=dholbert
fix_commit.author: Ting-Yu Lin

findings.title: Use-After-Free via stale pointer to CachedBAxisMeasurement
findings.message: The cachedMeasurement pointer is obtained at line 5671-5672 and stored in a local variable. Later, ReflowChild() is called at line 5685-5686, which may trigger MarkIntrinsicISizesDirty() -> MarkCachedGridMeasurementsDirty() that removes and frees the CachedBAxisMeasurement property from the frame. After ReflowChild() returns, the code at line 5693-5694 checks if cachedMeasurement is non-null and then calls cachedMeasurement->Update(), but the pointer is now dangling because the object it pointed to was freed during the reflow. This results in a heap-use-after-free write.
findings.suggestion: The cached pointer should not be stored across operations that may invalidate it. Re-fetch the property pointer from the frame after any operation that may have freed it (such as ReflowChild). Alternatively, move the variable declaration inside a scope that does not span the potentially-invalidating call.

ground_truth.root_cause: The vulnerability was introduced when Bug 1961424 changed CachedBAxisMeasurement from being stored by value (NS_DECLARE_FRAME_PROPERTY_SMALL_VALUE) to being stored by pointer (NS_DECLARE_FRAME_PROPERTY_DELETABLE). The old code stored the cache directly in the frame property by value and called SetProperty() each time to update it. The new code stores a pointer to a heap-allocated object, and the code pattern of caching the pointer in a local variable and using it after potentially-invalidating operations became unsafe because the pointed-to object could be freed during ReflowChild().

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable code path. Lines 5561-5562 obtain a pointer to GridItemCachedBAxisMeasurement from frame properties and store it in local variable 'cachedMeasurement'. Line 5576 calls parent->ReflowChild() which may trigger MarkIntrinsicISizesDirty() that removes the property. Lines 5594-5596 then use the stale cachedMeasurement pointer after the potential invalidation, calling cachedMeasurement.Update() on a potentially freed object.

This function removes/frees the CachedBAxisMeasurement property at line 6035 via RemoveProperty(). This can be called during ReflowChild() execution in MeasuringReflow, causing the cached measurement pointer stored earlier to become dangling.

This method is called at MeasuringReflow line 5596 on a potentially freed/invalidated cache object. The Update() call performs a write operation on freed memory, resulting in a heap-use-after-free vulnerability.
Calls MeasuringReflow at line 5909 during grid track sizing calculations. This is one of the primary call paths that triggers the vulnerable measuring reflow logic during grid layout computation.
Calls MeasuringReflow at line 6412 during baseline alignment calculations. This is another call path that can trigger the vulnerable code when computing item baselines in the grid layout algorithm.
